speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for describing your symptoms. To better understand your condition, can you tell me how long you have been experiencing the rectal bleeding, and is the blood bright red or dark?

speaker: Patient
text: 45-year-old female. The patient reports a 2-week history of rectal bleeding occurring daily with bowel movements. She denies any pain with defecation and does not present with any other complaints.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you noticed any unintended weight loss, fatigue, or changes in your bowel habits, such as constipation or diarrhea, over the past two weeks? REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC), Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP), and Tumor Markers (CEA, CA 19-9).

speaker: Doctor
text:
Given the normal blood work but the presence of daily rectal bleeding and a palpable mass, have you noticed any narrowing of your stool or changes in its shape? Also, is there any family history of colorectal cancer or inflammatory bowel disease?

REQUEST TEST: Colonoscopy with biopsy.

speaker: Doctor
text: This is confusing; the normal colonoscopy and blood work do not align with a palpable rectal mass and daily bleeding. Given the discrepancy, can you confirm if the mass feels fixed or mobile, and have you had any recent trauma or surgery to the pelvic region? REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic MRI. DIAGNOSIS READY: Rectal Polypoid Mass (likely benign adenoma or lipoma requiring excision).
